audit.whatIsWrong: Meditate is a channel and Mel's Solar Snare cancels it. The kit flags it 'channel: interruptible - any CC cancels it', Solar Snare is flagged hardCC, and _missing-interactions.json states it outright: 'Master Yi's Meditate (W) is a channel - your Solar Snare (E) cancels it.' Neither the spikes, the wants, the whys nor the prose mentions it anywhere.
audit.why: It is the one moment in the matchup where spending the root offensively is correct, and the entry's standing instruction is the exact opposite - 'At 6 never waste the root on poke', 'hold E for his commit', 'E and W held for his engage'. A player following the entry watches a full Meditate resolve with their root available. Cancelling it denies the heal and the Double Strike stacks it was banking.
audit.corrected: Meditate is a channel, so a Solar Snare root cancels the heal outright - the one time spending it early pays.

audit.whatIsWrong: Highlander grants immunity to slows and the entry never says so. Riot: 'making him immune to all slowing effects'. Solar Snare roots at its centre but only SLOWS in the surrounding area.
audit.why: This splits Mel's single CC ability in half at exactly level 6. From the moment Highlander is up, clipping him with the outer field achieves nothing - only a dead-centre hit still holds him, because a root is an immobilise rather than a slow. That is a precise aiming requirement that arrives on a specific timer, and it is the difference between peeling a diving Yi and watching him walk through the field.
audit.corrected: At 6 Highlander makes him immune to slows, so only the centre root of Solar Snare holds him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (E Solar Snare: 'rooting those at its center while the area around it slows')

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late instructs the reader to 'reflect a burst window with W'. Master Yi has no projectile anywhere in his kit - the flags across his five abilities are dash, untargetable, heal, channel, trueDamage and slow. There is nothing for Rebuttal's reflect clause to return. Relatedly, whys[0] and early both call Rebuttal a 'zone' ('your W Rebuttal zone', 'Q volleys and your W zone'); it is a barrier around herself, and Mel's zone abilities are Q and E.
audit.why: Rebuttal is still the right button here - it prevents damage and grants move speed, which is exactly what you want against a melee burst dive. But a reader told to look for a reflect window will hold it for a cast that never comes and eat the all-in with it unspent. The 'zone' framing also misattributes why levels 1-2 are safe: it is the 950 range on Radiant Volley and her 550 auto, not anything W does.
audit.corrected: Blank his burst with Rebuttal; the early safety comes from Radiant Volley's 950 range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/masteryi.json (no projectile flag on any slot)

audit.whatIsWrong: Alpha Strike's untargetability is only ever alluded to - whys[6] mentions 'his Alpha dodges' - and its consequence for Golden Eclipse is never stated. Riot: 'Master Yi teleports across the battlefield with blinding speed ... while simultaneously becoming untargetable.'
audit.why: Golden Eclipse strikes everyone carrying Overwhelm regardless of distance, on a 120s cooldown at rank 1. Fired while he is inside Alpha Strike it finds nothing. Since Alpha Strike is also how he opens every engage, the instinctive moment to detonate is precisely the wrong one.
audit.corrected: Hold Golden Eclipse until Alpha Strike ends - he is untargetable throughout it.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere in the entry. Alpha Strike is 20/19.5/19/18.5/18 and, per Riot, 'Basic attacks reduce Alpha Strike's cooldown.' Meditate is 10 flat, Highlander 85.
audit.why: 20 seconds at rank 1 is a long window for an ability the entry treats as omnipresent from level 3 - the reader is told the free lane is simply over, when in fact two thirds of it is still free if they count. The auto-attack reduction is the qualifier that stops that becoming false comfort: the more he is allowed to farm uninterrupted, the faster it returns.
audit.corrected: Alpha Strike 20s at rank 1, cut down by his basic attacks.

audit.why: 43.81% over 210 games - the second-largest sample in my slice and solid enough to trust. It matches the shape of the entry: Mel owns levels 1-2, Yi owns everything from his first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.spikes[] has 3 entries where the schema expects 4, and spikes[2].when is 'Full Overwhelm stacks' rather than an item or level milestone like every other matchup in the file.
audit.why: The missing beat is his first item, which the entry's own prose calls the point of no return ('You do not beat him in any 1v1 past his first item', 'first item makes his engage lethal'). The spike list omits the exact timing the text says decides the matchup.
